Sprit of the Hour
Soon as the sound had ceased whose thunder filled
The abysses of the sky, and the wide earth,
100 There was a change . . . the impalpable thin air
And the all-circling sunlight were transformed,
As if the sense of love, dissolved in them,
Had folded itself round the spherèd world.
 My vision then grew clear, and I could see
105 Into the mysteries of the universe.
 Dizzy as with delight I floated down,
Winnowing the lightsome air with languid plumes,

 Listen!] Nbk 9; Listen; 1820, 1839.
 The Spirit of the Hour reports back on the journey undertaken under Prometheus’s order at
III iii 64ff., and thus provides a second perspective, following that of the Spirit of the Earth, on the
momentous changes following the liberation of Prometheus and his reunion with Asia.
 I.e. the sound of the shell (cp. lines 54–7 above).
 sky,] Nbk 9; sky 1820, 1839.

energy, and the spirit of animation; cp. I 831–2, II v 26–30.
